One character in this work is honored for his crusade against street spitting, while another character claims to know a song which drives people to fall dead if they bear the plague. In addition to Gustaf Sondelius and Almus Pickerbaugh, this novel includes Joyce Lanyon, who marries the protagonist after she is saved in St. Hubert. A germ-cultured cigarette causes the death of Leora Tozer, while its protagonist is beaten to the publishing punch on the X Principle by D'Herelle. The protagonist eventually moves to Vermont, where founds a laboratory with Terry Wickett. Name this novel by Sinclair Lewis about a doctor who returns to a life of research.

The protagonist of this work promises a twelve-year-old "a kingdom," which later manifests itself as promises of "castles in the air." A fire in this work causes two infant twins to be killed when they drink milk addled by fever. Kaia Fosli is an assistant to the this work's central character, who fears that Ragnar Brovik will eclipse him in his profession, which calls on him to put a ceremonial object on the weather vane of a cathedral. The end of this work sees the central character climb the high central spire of his home to lay a ceremonial wreath, but fall to his death. Name this Henrik Ibsen play whose title character is the architect Halvard Solness.

This character owns "the nicest little black bitch of pointer" the owner of Barton Park has ever seen, and he promises to bring another character a horse from his estate at Somersetshire. He leaves during a heavy rain after his first appearance, in which he appears in hunting garb and assists a character with a twisted ankle. He eventually marries the rich Miss Grey after losing the allowance he received from a relative who had gotten wind of his affair with the ward of Colonel Brandon. Name this dashing rogue who is distrusted by Elinor and who throws over Marianne Dashwood in Jane Austen's Sense & Sensibility.

This play's chorus refers to a character "sprung of a dragon" who is "a savage monster in his very mien... Like some murderous giant pitted against heaven" before they summon an earthquake and raze his palace. A tree is bent down to allow that character to sit atop the forest, and he had earlier demanded the cutting of another character's sacred locks. Tiresias' criticisms of those who refuse to engage in the rites prevents his demise, while Cadmus is presented with the head of his grandson by his daughter Agave, who joined the maenads in ripping him apart. Name this play which ends with Dionysus' vengeance on Pentheus and the royal family of Thebes, a work of Euripides.

In one section of this work, a man married to a relative of the fire god is "seven times captured, seven times freed!" One character in this work defeats six generals while passing through five gates; after that character's death his spirit possesses Lu Meng at a banquet. A hilarious scene in this novel sees one character chase another around a garden with a spear after catching the latter embracing Diao Chan. Later in this novel, Fledgling Phoenix recommends the services of Sleeping Dragon to a man who'd made an oath in a peach garden with Zhang Fei and Guan Yu. Identify this classic Luo Guanzhong novel whose title entities are led by Sun Quan, Liu Bei, and Cao Cao.

One of this author's works stars the son of a priest of the Hill people who travels across the river Ou-dis-sun on a "god-road" to the Dead Place after having a vision of the Great Burning. This author of that post-apocalyptic story wrote about falling in love with "the snakeskin-titles of mining claims" in a poem that ends with the line "Bury my heart at Wounded Knee". Jack Ellyat and Clay Wingate are among the narrators of this man's epic poem about the Civil War, and he also wrote a story in which Mr. Scratch puts Jabez Stone on trial. Name this author of "By the Waters of Babylon", "American Names", John Brown's Body, and "The Devil and Daniel Webster".

This man wrote of a figure whose "lucid essence flames with lightnings" as he tells God that "Of light drawn from the holy fount" will "all time and all space" braid him a mystic crown and that "pain is the only nobility." That figure, the Poet, appears in "Benediction" as well as a poem wherein he is compared to a "prince of the clouds" who pathetically lets his "great white wings" drag after sailors catch him. This man also created a character who "dreams of scaffolds as he smokes his hookah pipe"; that figure is Ennui, who is known to the hypocrite twin. Name this author of "The Albatross" and "To the Reader", poems in his Flowers of Evil.

One work by this author notes that "the sword outwears its sheath / And the soul wears out the breast" before stating that "the night was made for loving / And the day returns too soon". The central figure of another of his poems exhibits "that tender light / Which heaven to gaudy day denies" and is compared to "the night / Of cloudless climes and starry skies". This author also wrote a long poem about a Spaniard who escapes from a seraglio and fights in the siege of Ismail while repeatedly being seduced. Identify this author of "So we'll go no more a-roving", "She walks in Beauty", and Don Juan, who created a namesake hero in his "Childe Harold's Pilgrimage".

In one of this man's works, Maria de Gloria becomes a teacher after Josemar leaves the town of Cocota. Pozzi tries to ransom Alejandro and W218 is seduced and betrayed in another of his novels. Big Fanny kills her lover Francisco Paez in a novel which sees Celina criticize Nene for her letters about her brother Juan Carlos Etchepare. The author of Blood of Requited Love, Pubis Angelical, and Heartbreak Tango, this man wrote a novel wherein Valentin Paz serves as a cellmate for Luis Molina, while in another novel, Mita tells the stories of films to her son Toto. Name this author of Betrayed by Rita Hayworth and Kissed by the Spider Woman.

One character in this work sells her diamonds to aid Maxime de Traille. A man's criminal brands are exposed when drinking coffee prepared by Madame Michonneau shortly after he engineered the death of Victorine Taillefer's brother. Only the protagonist and Bianchon are present at the title character's funeral, while Gondureau confirms that Trompe-la-Mort and Vautrin are the same person. Madame de Bauseant encourages this novel's protagonist to pay court to Delphine du Nucingen, who, along with her sister, bankrupts the title character with her extravagant lifestyle. Name this novel which sees Eugene de Rastignac befriend the title character.

One character in this work calls Europe "a great big auction" before relating a story about encountering a child prostitute in Marrakech. Dr. Baugh prescribes morphine for that character, who has a sister named "Miss Sally" and asks another of this work's characters if "chasin' poon-tang" resulted in his sprained ankle. Another character in this play drinks until he hears a "click" in his head, is disgusted with the world's "mendacity", and never came to terms with Skipper's homosexuality. Mae and Gooper scheme to receive the inheritance of the cancer-stricken Big Daddy in, which play about Brick and Maggie Pollitt, a work of Tennessee Williams?
Cat on a Hot Tin Roof

This author's later works include one about a character who repeatedly discovers that he just doesn't notice other people, driving his lover Maggie to suicide. That character visits a concentration camp with Holga and sees some of his associates targeted in the Red Scare and is named Quentin. This author of After the Fall wrote a play that sees a character die saying only "more weight" as stones are piled on top of him; that man is named Giles Corey. That play begins as Tituba has taken three girls to the forest and concludes with the trial of John Proctor name this author of a play set during the Salem witch trials, The Crucible.

John Hakac claimed that this poem's "organically complete" third stanza contains "three distinct phases of love". Its speaker makes a comparison to "a magic lantern" which "threw the nerves in patterns on a screen" and describes "the voices dying with a dying fall / Beneath the music from a farther room". Its speaker admits that he is "not Prince Hamlet, nor was meant to be" and says he "should have been a pair of ragged claws / Scuttling across the floors of silent seas". Opening with the line "Let us go then, you and I," it describes the speaker's distaste for women who "come and go / Talking of Michelangelo." identify this poem by T.S. Eliot.
The Love Song of J. Alfred Prufrock

One work by this man sees the philosopher d'Astarac die in a house-fire after the Jew Mosaide kills Maitre Jerome, the tutor of the protagonist Jacques Menetrier. Another of his novels features such characters as the chemist Prince Istar and the librarian Julien Sariette; that novel sees Maurice d'Esparvieu's guardian Arcade lead a rebellion against Ialdabaoth. This author also wrote novels about a philologist who obsesses over the Golden Legend and about a group led by Draco the Great who were accidentally baptized by the monk Mael. Name this author of At the Sign of the Reine Pedauque, The Revolt of the Angels, The Crime of Sylvester Bonnard, and Penguin Island.

One section of this work asserts that God experiences all moments in one and that time is a "distention" of the soul. Its thirteen book argues that truth is an assembly of fragments of eternal memories of God. Its third book describes a study of Hortensius that spurred a turn towards wisdom and away from the pleasures of the flesh. In book eight of this work, a small child inspires the narrator to closely read Romans which inspires him to listen to his mother Monica and convert from Manichaeism to Christianity. Name this autobiographical work that describes the conversion of Saint Augustine of Hippo.

This author's first novel is divided into two parts, the first of which ends with Martin being stabbed by a man who writes a report on Vietnam War propaganda named Eugene Dawn. He also created a character that moves in with the bedridden amputee Paul Rayment in one novel and, in another, becomes famous for The House on Eccles Street. This creator of Elizabeth Costello wrote novels about a professor who regularly meets with the prostitute Soraya but loses his job after a charge of sexual harassment and about a harelipped gardener who takes his mother's ashes to St. Albert. Name this author who won Booker Prizes for Disgrace and The Life and Times of Michael K.

This character describes being "Venerien in feeling" and having a "Marcien" heart before noting that she was born a Taurus. This character, who repeatedly quotes from Ptolemy's Almagest and compares herself to barley bread, is said to know of "remedies of love, perchance" and to have a confidant that shares her name. She punches another character after tearing a few pages out of Valerie and Theofraste, after which that character hits her so hard she goes half-deaf. She meets that character, Jankin, at her fourth husband's funeral. Name this character who tells of a knight given a year and a day to find out what women want in her namesake Canterbury Tale.

In "Dying is an Art," George Steiner refers to this poem as "the Guernica of modern poetry." Its third stanza describes a place "where it pours bean green over blue / In the waters off beautiful Nauset." Its speaker claims "The black telephone's off at the root" and "the voices just can't worm through." Its addressee is later told about villagers who "are dancing and stamping on you" and that "there's a stake in your fat black heart." Its speaker says "I think I may well be a Jew" before bitterly noting that "Every woman adores a Fascist." identify this poem that opens "you do not do, you do not do," in which Sylvia Plath tells the title figure "you bastard, I'm through."

One character in this work prays to "merchante Fortune" after asking "be these the wretches we played dice for?" While wooing his future wife, the protagonist claims "a good heart" is "the sun and not the moon" and asks "come, your broken music." After receiving a gift of tennis balls, the title figure claims he will make them cannon balls, an image echoed in a speech beginning "once more unto the breach, dear friends." The protagonist foils the Southampton plot, while Pistol and Bardolph recall the title character's youth and the death of Falstaff. Name this play whose title character talks of "we few, we happy few" in his St. Crispin's Day Speech, a work of William Shakespeare.

One character created by this man weaves a series of shawls depicting her husband's rise to power and overthrow by Raza Hyder. Rani and Iskander Harappa are found in a book by this man that also features Sufiya, whose outbreaks of violence lead to her beheading her husband Omar before exploding. He also created a character who dreams of Abu Simbel's deal with "the Messenger", Mahound, and who shoots Whisky Sisodia before throwing Alleluia Cone off a roof. This author of Shame also wrote a novel that begins with a hijacked plane exploding over the English Channel. Identify this author of that book about Saladin Chamcha and Gibreel Farishta, The Satanic Verses.

One character in this work treasures a "high-flown" love letter given to her at a dance by a medical student. This work's narrator pens a satirical novel about, and considers sending a fur collar to, an officer who shoves him without comment in a billiard hall. In its second section, "Apropos of the Wet Snow", its protagonist invites himself to a dinner party planned by his schoolmate Simonov for another schoolmate, Zverkov, but shows up an hour early and insults everyone. Ending shortly after the prostitute Liza realizes the protagonist is incapable of love, identify this novella that begins "I am a sick man, I am a spiteful man", a work of Fyodor Dostoevsky.

One work by this author opens "breathe, you invisible poem!", and another considers a youth who "climbs alone, on the mountains of primal grief." Another poem by this author observes a "torso" that "is still suffused with brilliance from inside" and affirms that "we cannot know his legendary head" before concluding "you must change your life." This poet gave as exemplar of unrequited love the example of Gastara Stampa. This author of "The Archaic Torso of Apollo" began his best-known collection "Who, if I cried out, would hear me among the angelic orders?" name this author of the Sonnets to Orpheus and Duino Elegies.

One scene in this work describes a man earlier arrested at a post office who went mad from studying too much. Reverend Hammond places a cross around the neck of this work's protagonist, who had earlier discussed robbing a deli. Its protagonist tells Britten that the Jan Erlone is Jewish in an attempt to frame him. One character in this work announces that he has sent some Ping-Pong tables to the South Side Boys' Club, but Boris A. Max later reveals him to be a racist slum lord. The title character kills Bessie and throws her down an air shaft after a reporter discovers an earring among the ashes of Mary Dalton in, which work about Bigger Thomas by Richard Wright?

One character in this novel wakes up every morning to see the dark-blue-bordered handkerchief with which she smothered a baby, while another character is forced to wear a heavy picture of a black poodle around her neck. The spymaster Afranius serves a character who insists on being addressed as "Hegemon" and who is also served by Mark the Ratkiller. In its opening section, the head of MASSOLIT is beheaded by a trolley in front of Ivan Bezdomny. Its first title character wrote a novel about Pontius Pilate and Christ and eventually leaves Moscow with the other title character and Woland, who is Satan in disguise. Name this Mikhail Bulgakov novel.

In one work by this author, a character repeatedly claims to need to "get down to Sidcup" and retrieve papers which would prove that his name is "Mac Davies" rather than "Bernard Jenkins". That character is later evicted after Mick smashes a bust of Buddha while yelling at Aston. Another of this man's plays is set at Meg and Peter Boles's boardinghouse and sees Lulu give a drum to Stanley, who is taken away after the title event by Goldberg and McCann. A third play by this man sees two men argue about the phrase "light the kettle"; that work ends with Ben aiming a gun at Gus. Name this author of The Caretaker, The Birthday Party, and The Dumbwaiter.

One of his poems notes that "Numb Antony" "lies like a copper palm" by a "hot sea and a river" and another poem claims "the great hexameters come to the conclusions of exhausted surf" and that "the classics can console/But not enough." In one work by this poet of "Egypt Tobago" and "Sea Grapes", Basil forces the corporal to admit his love of Africa and Mostique tells Makak to profit from his healing powers. Another of his plays sees Ma Kilman heal Philoctete and centers around Achille and Omeros, who are fisherman living on St. Lucia. Name this Carribean-born author of Dream on Monkey Mountain and Omeros.

Near the end of its first section, one character helps a pair of children sleep by wrapping a boar's head in her shawl. One character in this work imagines the human mind as a progression through the alphabet and regrets being stuck at Q; that character wanders around quoting from "The Charge of the Light Brigade". Prue and Andrew die during its second section, "Time Passes", while its first section, "The Window", sees Paul Rayley and Minta Doyle get engaged. Lily Briscoe finally finishes a painting in its last section, during which Cam and James finally make the title voyage with Mr. Ramsay. Name this stream-of-consciousness novella by Virginia Woolf.

One work by this man dissects the relationship between assent, apprehension, and inference regarding religion. He argued for the "cultivation of the intellect" and for a division of labor between teaching and research in the titular institution in another book. Another work by this author of the Grammar of Assent is a response to Charles Kingsley and claims there are strains of Arianism in the faith that he abandoned. This author of "The Idea of the University" converted from Anglicanism and wrote a poem that inspired an Elgar oratorio. Name this English Cardinal who wrote "Dream of Gerontius" and described his conversion to Catholicism in Apologia Pro Vita Sua.

In one poem, this author asserts that "heroes seek release / From dusty bondage into luminous air". Another of her works thrice repeats the couplet "We were very tired, we were very merry-- / We had gone back and forth all night upon the ferry". She wrote of viewing "three long mountains and a wood" in a work in which she sees God's face after being revived by rain. The couplet "Safe upon the solid rock the ugly houses stand: / Come and see my shining palace built upon the sand!" is found in her most famous collection, which begins "My candle burns at both ends". Name this author of "Recuerdo" and "Renascence", as well as the collection A Few Figs from Thistles.

Near the beginning of this work, the narrator looks down into a "black and lurid tarn" in an attempt to "annihilate [the] capacity for sorrowful impression" of the title object. This work's narrator remembers a "perversion" of "the wild air of the last waltz of von Weber" being played by a character who sings a song called "The Haunted Palace". Its narrator later reads a novel in which the knight Ethelred kills a dragon and receives a shield, Launcelot Canning's The Mad Trist. Late in this work, a pair of doors burst open to reveal Madeleine, after which Roderick dies of terror. Name this story which ends with the collapse of the title structure, a work of Edgar Allan Poe.
The Fall of the House of Usher

This poem is dedicated to "a certain poetess" who asked "Who'll grip and tackle the job unafraid?" in "Who's for the Game?". Its speaker describes an event that occurs "at every jolt" as "Obscene as cancer, bitter as the cud / Of vile, incurable sores on innocent tongues". Its subjects, who became "deaf even to the hoots / Of tired, outstripped Five-Nines", are said to be "Bent double, like old beggars under sacks". Its second stanza describes an "ecstasy of fumbling", after which a man plunges at its speaker, "guttering, choking, drowning". Its title is described as "the old Lie" and is taken from Horace. Identify this poem about a gas attack, written by Wilfred Owen.

At the end of this work's second act, one character grabs another and sings, "We are the boys / That fears no noise / Where the thundering cannons roar," while in this play's first act, that character sings about the Three Pigeons alehouse. Another character in this work instructs his servants Roger and Diggory to prepare for a "table exercise." Avoiding a trip to Aunt Pedigree's house allows Constance Neville to steal jewels and elope with George Hastings in this work, which also sees Tony Lumpkin trick its male protagonist into believing the house he seeks is merely an inn. Charles Marlow believes Kate Hardcastle to be a servant in which play by Oliver Goldsmith?

Marini is found dead on a beach by Klaios, a villager of Xiros, in one of this man's stories, while in another Rice is forced to play the part of John Howell. Irene and the unnamed narrator lose their home in one of his short stories, "Casa tomada," and in a story from the same collection, a tiger roams around Rema's house. In addition to Bestiario, he wrote a story in which Roberto Michel photographs a woman and a boy caught in an illicit act, The Blow-Up. In another of his works, Horatio Oliveira searches for La Maga throughout France and South America. Name this Argentine author of Hopscotch.

This author wrote "When you came, you were like red wine and honey" in a poem from the series "Two Speak Together" that was dedicated to Ada Dwyer Russell and titled "A Decade". The title objects of one of this poet's works have "forgotten [their] Eastern origin" and are "a curiously clear-cut, candid flower" that appears in "great puffs" across New England. She also imagined a man "fighting with the Duke in Flanders" while she walks "up and down" the "garden-paths" in another of her poems. Name this author of such collections as What's O'Clock and A Dome of Many-Colored Glass, which contain Imagist poems like "Lilacs" and "Patterns".

In the beginning of this play, two characters repeat "Let us bolt!" and in another part, one character threatens to tear out another's eyelashes; in response, the other says he will slit his gullet. The orchestra area represents the Pnyx at Athens, and the protagonists attempt to impress another by pointing out the differences between the two. Two slaves find that another character is doomed to be replaced, and after Nicias brings him some wine and the oracle, Demosthenes tells Agoracritus, the sausage-seller, that it is his destiny to overtake the Paphlagonian as ruler of Demos. Identify this play in which Aristophanes derides Cleon by portraying him as a leather-cutter.

A man from Black Bear Lake becomes engaged to Irene Scheerer in a work by this man that details six encounters between Judy Jones and Dexter Green. In another of his stories, the sudden arrival of Duncan Schaeffer and Lorraine Quarles horrifies Marion Peters, thus preventing Charlie Wales from recovering his daughter Honoria. Another of his protagonists learns from Kismine that Percy Washington's parents shoot down airmen who observe the Montana mountain that holds a certain gemstone. Name this author of "Winter Dreams" and "Babylon Revisited" who told of John Unger in "The Diamond as Big as the Ritz" and penned The Great Gatsby.

Benedetto Croce claimed this work's fortune is comparable to a smiling and lovely girl. It remarks that men should extract their wings from the "loving birdlime." One character builds a bridge to atone for his drunken murder of a princess mourning Zerbino after he quarrels over Doralice with Mandricardo. That character is killed by a man who earlier rode a hippogryph to save a girl who chooses Medoro after seducing Rinaldo and the title character. Featuring Bradamante, Rogero, and Angelica, name this poem about a paladin of Charlemange by Ludovico Ariosto.

[5,5] Among the swords credited to Wayland is Durandal, which was said to have been owned both by a Frankish paladin who died at Roncesvalles and a Trojan prince whose brother was Paris. For five points each, name them.

This man told of Quaquaro, the steward of Sidonie Knobbe and the Hassenreuter family in one play. Streckmann blackmails and rapes the title character of another work, who bears Flamm's child but tries to marry Keil. Helene commits suicide after she learns that Alfred Loth leaves her because of her family's alcohol problems in his first play Before Dawn. In another of his plays, Old Baumert vomits after being unable to digest dog-meat, and that plays sees Becker and Jaeger lead the titular workers to revolt against the oppression of Dreissiger. Identify this man wrote about the plight of the titular Silesians in The Weavers.

The protagonist of this work fights a gang of teenagers after a pathetic show of strength at an arcade. While searching for an escaped lunatic the protagonist recalls his betrayal of Kikuhiko, whom he later meets in a gay bar. Another character in this book describes her theory of the "pluralistic universe." The protagonist vomits in front of his class after drinking away his troubles at the home of his girlfriend Himiko. The protagonist of this work longs to travel to Africa, but becomes a tour guide after accepting the responsibility of his family. Identify this novel whose protagonist Bird has a child with a Brain hernia, a work by Kenzaburo Oe.

This director ended one of his films with a scene where money flies out of a suitcase and the criminal Johnny Clay is arrested at the airport. Another of his films sees Colonel Dax angrily refers to General Broulard as "a degenerate, sadistic old man" after failing to stop the execution of three soldiers for cowardice. This director of The Killing and Paths of Glory is better known a film that features Heywood Floyd's search for TMA-1. That film by this man opens with a shot of the sun rising over the earth rising over the moon as Also Sprach Zarathustra plays and ends with Dave Bowman becoming a star-child. Name this director of 2001: A Space Odyssey.

At one point in this work, its protagonist, who is judged to be "no vulgar assassin", listens to the "audible music" of gnats and dragonflies after undergoing an "awful disturbance of his organic system" and later blesses the sand and judges the wind to sound like Aeolian harps upon reaching shore. Earlier, its protagonist had been given information about dry, flammable timber by a man later revealed to be a Federal scout. In the final scene of this work, the protagonist begins to greet his wife, but is interrupted by a "stunning blow upon the back of the neck." name this Ambrose Bierce short story revealed to be a dream taking place during Peyton Farquhar's hanging.
An Occurrence at Owl Creek Bridge

This author asserts that while one may learn something new from a cookbook, reading Milton will result in higher capacity to sympathize with the infinite, which makes Milton an example of the "literature of power". Another work by this author compares the sound of wheels during a funeral procession and a woman's sigh before fainting to the title event, which interrupts a moment in "the world of darkness" caused by a certain literary murder. This author of "On the Knocking at the Gate in Macbeth" also wrote the Gothic novel Klosterheim and a memoir about the "pains" and "pleasures" of a certain drug. Name this author of Confessions of an English Opium-Eater.

This novel's protagonist meets Fanny dressed as an angel and gives his name as "Negro" shortly before his second encounter with the scrawny Giacomo. This work's protagonist learns horseriding from Mack, whose fiance Clara Pollunder tries to rape him, while the fondness of Grete Mitzelbach and Therese nets him a job at Hotel Occidental. Delamarche and Robinson abuse the protagonist of this novel, who goes to the Nature Theatre of Oklahoma. Early on the protagonist is taken in by his wealthy Uncle Jacob and endures the Stoker's complaints after seeing the Statue of Liberty with a sword. Name this novel about Karl Rossman's adventures in the title country by Franz Kafka.

This author described how Beckett and Borges succeeded Joyce and Kafka as "technically contemporary" writers in an essay called "The Literature of Exhaustion". The protagonist of a novel by this man gets a job at Wicomico State College and has an affair with Joe Morgan's wife Rennie before returning to a state of "psychological paralysis". After writing about Jacob Horner in The End of the Road, this author wrote a novel about a man tutored by Henry Burlingame who marries Joan Toast after becoming Poet Laureate of Maryland. Name this author who satirized the modern university in Giles Goat-Boy and who wrote that aforementioned novel, The Sot-Weed Factor.

The protagonist of one of this man's works erects a sign claiming that that story's title figure will ascend to heaven from a pond on the third day of the third month. The central figure of another of his stories watches his daughter and her pet monkey burn to death in a carriage after torturing his apprentices to capture their suffering while painting the title work. This author of "Dragon: the Old Potter's Tale" also wrote a story in which a servant steals the robe of an old woman who collects hair from corpses at the titular gate and a story consisting of seven different accounts of the murder of Takehiro. Identify this Japanese author of "Hell Screen", "Rashomon", and "In a Grove".

In one poem in this collection, the speaker derides poets who rely on Petrarchan oxymorons like "fair storms and freezing fires", preferring to use only his "trembling voice" to display "all the map of my state". This work's first poem describes how the speaker "sought fit words to paint the blackest face of woe" before his Muse says "Fool… look in thy heart and write." Its most famous poem opens with the line "With how sad steps, O Moon, thou climbst the skies", while its dedicatee is believed to be Penelope Devereux. Identify this collection of 11 songs and 108 sonnets, a work by Sir Philip Sidney about two star-crossed and star-named lovers.

This poem recalls a time of innocence when one figure was "playing with blue plums" or walking on stilts, while the narrator was pulling flowers. This poem recounts how "at fifteen I stopped scowling" and "desired my dust to be mingled with yours." That time of innocence is described as when "my hair was still cut straight across my forehead," which must have been long before the addressee went to "the river of swirling eddies." Its narrator, who "at fourteen... Married My Lord you," promises that she "will come out to meet you/ as far as Cho-fu-sa." name this poem, translated from Li Po by Ezra Pound.
The River Merchant's Wife: A Letter

This work's title character tells his wife he needed her "as the abyss across which my body must be drawn." He asks "the ghostly one" to release his "shadow" after the Aide-de-Camp wonders what to do about an "invasion" of women chanting a dirge. This work sees young girls imitate British mannerisms and mock the sexuality of the Christian constable Amusa. This play opens with a discussion between the Praise Singer and the title character in the market district ruled by Iyaloja, who berates the title character when she finds him chained by Simon Pilkings, obligating his son Olunde to take his life. Name this play about the title Yoruban, a work of Wole Soyinka.

One man from this country wrote the novel Paradiso. Another writer from this country wrote a novel featuring the relationship of Vivian Smith Corona and Eribo as well as the section "Headcracker", wherein Bustrófedon becomes a Christ figure. One writer from this country wrote of Dr. Ogé curing Esteban of his asthma and Sofia succumbing to the advances of Victor Hugues in one novel. Besides the authors of Three Trapped Tigers and Explosion in a Cathedral, a poet from this nation wrote of how he "cultivates a white rose" and is "an honest man from where the palm trees grow" in "Guantanamera." name this country home to Alejo Carpentier and Jose Marti.

One character in this play tells his father "timid innocence" was never known to suddenly become "extreme licence." The title character apostrophizes her father in telling him "Venus' wrath has doomed your race", shortly before she castigates her maid. A half-bull half-dragon is summoned on a favour owed by Neptune to kill a character that discusses his desire to leave Troezen with Théramène and loves Ismène's friend Aricie. Oenone convinces the title character to tell her husband that his son forced himself on her. Name this play in which the title character is destroyed by her love for Thésée 's son Hippolyte, a work of Jean Racine.

In a note published with this poem, its author lamented how "a thousand circlets spread, / and each mis-shape the other". Its speaker compares a fountain to "chaffy grain beneath the thresher's flail" after describing "forests ancient as the hills" and "gardens bright with sinuous rills". Its speaker tells of a vision of an Abyssinian maid playing a dulcimer and singing of Mount Abora and desires to build a structure featuring "caves of ice" near the river Alph so that people will cry "Beware! Beware! / His flashing eyes, his floating hair!" name this poem in which "a stately pleasure-dome" is decreed in Xanadu by the title emperor, a work of Samuel Taylor Coleridge.

This author wrote a novella in which Linus Steinman attempts to find his number-reciting parrot Bruno with the help of a beekeeping retired detective that is implied to be Sherlock Holmes. One of his characters investigates both Alter Litvak's attempt to bomb the Dome of the Rock and the murder of Mendel Shpilman with his half-Tlingit partner Berko Shemets in a Jewish settlement in Sitka, Alaska. This author of The Final Solution created Meyer Landsman and wrote a novel about the creators of Amazing Midget Radio Comics, Luna Moth, and The Escapist. Identify this author of The Yiddish Policemen's Union and The Amazing Adventures of Kavalier & Clay.

After World War II, this man wrote two books decrying colonialism titled after "the primeval forest." This man delivered a speech that cites the dangerousness of strontium-90 to health studies of residents nearby Nagasaki to conclude the abolishment of nuclear proliferation will be similar to "rays of sunlight" that humanity hopes for in his "A Declaration of Conscience" speech. His doctrine of "To be in awe of the mystery of life" or the "reverence of life" led him to write The Decay and Restoration of Civilization. This Bach-enthusiast and author of The Mystery of the Kingdom of God and The Psychiatric Study of Jesus also wrote a book that attempts to give a fact based biography of the titular New Testament figure. Name this theologian and physician who wrote The Quest for the Historical Jesus.

A poet with this surname described those who find "a famished kitten on the step" and save it "from the fury of the street." Another poet with this surname wrote a poem whose addressee's "lover threw wild hands towards the sky;" the speaker in that poem is repeatedly told "do not weep." The latter wrote about "three little birds in a row" who laugh at a man trying to sing. A poet with this surname wrote "Chaplinesque" and described "the dice of drowned men's bones" in "At Melville's Tomb." "A clang and clang of spear and shield" appears in another work, which describes a creature enjoying a dish that is bitter, just because it's his own heart. The magnum opus of another poet with this surname includes "Powhatan's Daughter" and "Cutty Sark." identify this surname shared by the authors of "War is Kind," "The Black Riders," and The Bridge, whose first names are Stephen and Hart.

In one play by this author, a couple utters the word "Sollocks" to prevent their arguments from getting out of hand. In another play, a character complains about a "gothic edition of Wembley Stadium" after discussing the affairs of Henry Lyppiatt. That play describes a sort of family formed by the members of Garry Essendine's crew, all of whom buy tickets to Africa, and was double-billed with this author's play This Happy Breed. Ruth gets killed driving a car sabotaged by the medium Madame Arcati in one play by this author, who loved having his characters tiptoe off-stage as the curtain dropped. In addition to writing Present Laughter and Private Lives, this author wrote about the Bliss family in one play and a play about Charles Condomine that takes its title from Shelley's "To a Skylark." identify this classy English dramatist who wrote Hay Fever and Blithe Spirit.

The first chapter of this novel ends with one character's purchase of a fifteen-cent can of sardines and observation of two large plumes of smoke in the distance. Chronologically earlier than that, another character is so disgusted by the menstrual cycle that he slaughters a farmer's sheep. A third character is so caught up in the mystery of his chicken-stealing Cavalryman grandfather that he does not care about his adulterous wife, who had committed suicide by jumping from a hotel window. A sexual misstep by the dietitian Miss Atkins leads to the ejection of the protagonist from his orphanage. Thus begins the protagonist's string of misfortunes, which include his murder of foster father Mr. McEachern, castration in the farm of Gail Hightower, and murder of Joanna Burden. Lena Grove searches for the father of her child in, what novel about Joe Christmas, written by William Faulkner?

A landmark study by Humbert has traced the non-usage of the dative case in this language during the medieval era, that medieval form of this language was used to inscribe a column found in Chatalar. The ancient form of this language confined the "free" word accent to its last syllable. The Balkan Sprachbund during the late Dark Ages mainly used Albanian and this other language. Pronouncing this language during that time period is illustrated by the Suda. When a word begins with a vowel in this language, you either form a spiritus lenis or a spiritus asper to pronounce that word. For forming superlative adjectives in this language, appending "tatos" to adjectives will do just fine. Identify this language, whose medieval version is called Byzantine, and whose ancient version was used by Pindar and Sapphro.

The tenth section of this work describes angels "weeping o'er the tomb/Where Thomas sleeps" That section also contains a scene where "the machine of the world" is explained to the protagonist, who learns about the Battle of Diu from his lover on Love Island. Earlier in this work, a woman wishes to be exiled in Siberia or Libya in the "lyric-tragic episode." An evil character in this work sends an ominous black cloud that "chill[s] the flesh and the hairs" of the main characters, who hear about the "Twelve of England," are aided by Monsayeed, and are betrayed by the Catual. In its fifth section, the Southern Cross and St. Elmo's Fire appear before the Great Adamastor does. The Olympian Gods convene at the behest of Bacchus, who views Vasco da Gama and his crew as too god-like for their own good. Identify this epic poem by Camoens, the national epic of Portugal.

One character in this novel smiles in such a way that her son secretly sends her gifts to make her smile for him. Another character wires his brother $100 and asks for a security question pertaining to a gift he once gave. A woman informs a sheriff about her broken jaw, which she received after being severely beaten by Mr. Edwards. That character sleeps with a man after drugging that man's brother, whom she had recently married. In this novel, an ex-boyfriend's seeking of solace in the church disgusts Abra Bacon, who learns from the Chinese housekeeper Lee about timshel, or choice of one's own moral destiny. Nine children are born to Liza, the wife of the narrator, who befriends the son of Cyrus and father of Caleb and Aron. Narrated by Samuel Hamilton and set in the Salinas Valley, name this novel about Adam Trask, written by John Steinbeck.

The film adaptation of this novel opens with shots of fingerprints and passport stamps. The protagonist is described in a dossier as an introvert who isn't socially inept, but does possess a "psychological venereal disease." At its end, a correspondence from his mother Shino reveals that he has been missing for seven years. Shortly before that, the title character begins to hemorrhage from pregnancy around the same time that the protagonist discovers that his failed crow-trap accumulates water. The "city woman" is contrasted with the title character, whose house is accessed by a rope ladder by the protagonist after he misses the last bus back from the coast. The title sand shoveller almost tempts her lover to give up entomology. Identify this novel about Niki Jumpei, the masterwork of Kobo Abe.

The protagonist of one novel by this author is ministered in his last moments by Father Anonymous and prostitutes Goody Pangall to Roger Mason to keep the latter working. In a Booker-winning novel, he created Zenobia Brocklebank, who is sought by Billy Rogers, who also seduces Reverend Colley, sparking the title transformation in Edmund Talbot on a ship-of-the-line. The former novel concerns the destruction of four pillars by the dean Joscelin, who is told by a vision to add the title structure to his church. This author's To the Ends of Earth trilogy opens with Rites of Passage. He also wrote about Lok and Fa, the last of the Neanderthals, and a novel concerning a creature who is fed a sow's head upon a stick. The Beast was created by, what author of The Spire, The Inheritors, and a novel about Jack, Ralph, and Piggy titled Lord of the Flies?

In the second scene of this play, a woman who loves the title character invites her governess to literally place her hand on her heart to see how it throbs for him. The primary female character, who is attended to by Elvire, is twice convinced that her lover has died; the second time, it is because his sword is triumphantly presented to her by Don Sanche. The title character takes a lesson from that second duel and doesn't kill his opponent, as he had in the first one that had been fought between Don Diegue and Don Gomes, whose daughter Chimène reluctantly agrees to marry the title character just as he's ordered to lead an expedition against the Moors. Identify this historical play set in Castille and written by Pierre Corneille.

One character in one of this author's novels gets a late night job at a variety store but falls asleep each night. Another character in that novel has both of his feet hoisted up by a rope in a cold shack, requiring amputation. In another of her novels, an soldier attempts to seduce a "Jasmine" whom he had met in the Blue Moon Cafe. In a short story, she described a boxing match between Marvin Macy and his ex-wife, who, seven years after meeting Cousin Lymon Willis, boards up the title establishment. The black cook Berenice takes care of Frankie Addams, who wishes to join her brother and his fiancee in one of her novels. She wrote about Miss Amelia Evans in one story and about Biff Brannon and Mick Kelly, attendees of the funeral of the mute Mr. Singer, in another. Identify this author of The Member of the Wedding, "The Ballad of the Sad Cafe," and The Heart is a Lonely Hunter.

One character in this play justifies a love affair by reminding the audience that in his youth, he was preoccupied by making a name for himself rather than finding love. The lover of that character hands him a medallion with the line "if you ever need my life, come take it" from his book Days and Nights. One character compares his mother's relationship with her lover to Gertrude's with Claudius; for that insolence, he gets run off stage when two red eyes and the smoke of sulphur are released during a performance. The sound of that character's suicide is compared to the pop of a cork by the doctor Dorn, who is attracted to Paulina. In this play, Medvedenko finally gets to marry Masha, who is still deeply in love with a successful writer who kills the title animal for Nina. When he realizes that Nina still loves Trigorin, Konstantin Treplev commits suicide. Identify this play by Anton Chekov.

One of this author's protagonists prostitutes herself in Nordstjärnan to dehumanize herself, such that she can exact revenge on her father's murderer Loewenthal. Besides writing "Emma Zunz," he examined the possibility that any object "can contain the seed of a possible Hell" in "Deutsches Requiem" and in a story about a coin minted in 1929 with letters N T etched on it, which the narrator uses to pay for a drink at a bar. This author describes a stone pillar in a Cairo mosque with the same properties as the demolished house of the second place winner of a literary prize. Other stories by this author of "The Zahir" include one about a boy who falls from his horse and recites specific passages from Pliny and one about a point that contains all other points, found in Carlos Daneri's basement. Identify this author of "Funes the Memorious" and "The Aleph," a blind Argentinian.
Jorge Francisco Isidoro Luis Borges Acevedo

In one section of this author's best known work, the eight-year old Jon lives an idyllic life with all his wishes gratified; we learn that both Jon and his mother survive despite the father being told he could save only one of them. Another of this author's characters absconds with his wife's pearls and runs off to South America with a dancer, but returns to that wife, Winifred. He included two interludes titled "Awakening" and "Indian Summer" in his magnum opus, in which Michael Mont is invited to see a picture gallery. This author described the wedding ceremony of June and the architect Phillip Bosinney, who dies after learning that his mistress Irene had been raped by her own husband, Soames. Old and Young Jolyon are major characters in this author's trilogy consisting of The Man of Property, In Chancery, and To Let. Identify this British author of The Forsyte Saga.

In this novel, radio and television broadcasts titled "The Norwegian Captain and the Tailor's Daughter" and "How Buckley Shot the Russian General" represent the protagonists. One couple in this novel briefly pause their lovemaking session to attend to their frightened child Jerry, after which they resume until the rooster crows. The fourth book of this novel consists of only one short chapter, in which the primary female character attempts to wake her husband, delivers her monologue, then disappears; to that end, the last sentence of this novel loops around the first. Shem, Shaun, and Issy are the children of the primary characters in this novel, a representation of Vico's New Science, which opens with the sentence "riverrun, Past Eve's and Adam's." Focusing on Anna Livia Plurabelle and her husband Humphrey Chimpden Earwicker, identify this experimental novel by James Joyce.

One part of this work is a critique of Tristes Tropiques that discusses the placing of the "Cerebral Savage" on the throne in the guise of "King Reason" and attacks Levi-Strauss's notion that humanity has spoiled the world and left behind only "remnants of the Garden of Eden." Another part of this book describes that to under social anthropology, it is necessary to not only understand "what ethnography is," but rather "what doing ethnography is." That part of this work asks "what is le penseur doing" and borrows a critical concept from Gilbert Ryle in order to analyze a wink. The last essay of this book contains a list of facts that describe the "dramatization of status concerns" infused in the titular activity on the island of Bali. Name this collection that contains the essay "Deep Play," which also puts forth the concept of thick description, written by Clifford Geertz.

In one non-canonical book of this name, all of the paper in a certain country is depleted, leading its ruler sentencing Jews to be crushed to death by elephant, all 500 of which end up getting drunk. The hero of another book of this name witnesses the dead bodies of several figures bearing amulets as idols of Jamnia and prays for them such that they might be free of sin. Eleazar and a woman with seven sons are martyrs present in that book of this name, which follows one which describes the foreskin restoration of Jews subject to Hellenization by Antiochus IV. The hero of these Deuterocanonical books founded the Hasmonean Dynasty and commemorated an eight-day long flame by celebrating Hanukkah. Identify these two books about a Judas who led a revolt against the Seleucids.

The title character of this play props himself up against a tree, proclaims that his feet have turned to stone and his "hands are gloved with lead" as he imagines a conversation with Death. A woman states "I hoped for cream, - you give me gruel," to which her suitor seductively says "Your throat I'd kiss it," driving her away. That suitor is the supposed author of a letter whose contents are recited to the primary female character in the dark, proving to her that the friend of Ligniere is not the true author. The title character recites the last word of a poem just as he stabs a man and later boastfully claims that he can deal with one hundred such men waiting in ambush. This play opens at the Hotel de Bourgogne and contains a balcony scene, where Christian's lines are spoken by his gigantic-nosed friend. Identify this play about a lover of Roxane, a historical drama by Edmond Rostand.

The first wife of one protagonist created by this novelist leaves him for a taxi driver after four years of marriage, but dies in childbirth. Though not Thomas Pynchon, this author created a character named V, who is so disgusted with Mr. Goodman's biography of his half-brother that he writes one himself. This author described the conspiracy between Axel Rex and his lover Margot Peters to use and ruin the wealthy Albert Albinus. This author of The Real Life of Sebastian Knight and Laughter in the Dark wrote about Victor Wind, the son of the title character, who is fired by Dr. Hagen from the faculty of Waindell College. He wrote about a production of The Enchanted Hunters put on by headmistress Miss Pratt in a novel whose central character murders Clare Quilty and lusts after nymphets like Dolores Haze. Identify this author of Pnin and a novel about Humbert Humbert, Lolita.

It is implied that the protagonist of this novel committed incest with a man she calls "Cousin Sandi." The worst character steals the protagonist's dresses and throws a rock at her forehead as they flee a burning house. This novel ends with the protagonist holding a candle and the garter key of Grace Poole. The servant girl Amelie has sex with an unnamed character, whose love the protagonist tries to gain using a magic potion brewed by the obeah-practicing Christophine. The sickly and unintelligent Pierre is the son of the certified madwoman Annette, whose stepson Richard Mason gets knifed by the protagonist, whose generic Englishman husband calls her his "Bertha." Antoinette Cosway is the protagonist of, what prequel to Jane Eyre written by Jean Rhys?

One character in this novel states that her motto is "only connect," in contrast to her husband's motto "concentrate." That woman appreciates "the outer world of telegram and anger" and expresses her disdain for Christmas during a shopping trip. The image of "goblins marching on the universe" permeates a performance of Beethoven's Fifth Symphony in this novel, whose minor characters include the sixteen-year old Tibby, Dolly's uncle Percy Cahill, and a former Cypriot prostitute named Jacky. The expiration of the lease on Wickham Place occurs before a marriage proposal in this novel, which ends after a former insurance agent is crushed by a bookcase and suffers a heart attack. Leonard Bast has a quick tumble with Helen, the sister of Margaret Schlegel, who moves into the title estate. Identify this book about the staunchly English Wilcoxes, written by E.M. Forster.

The protagonist of one of this author's novels picks up a discarded bouquet and hands it to his crush, whom he later spurns for her husband's mistress Rosanette. An unfinished novel of his concerns two characters that meet on a park bench and realize they are alike in every manner except for appearance. He wrote about a Hospitaller who kills his parents and ascends to heaven with a leper, and about the death of John the Baptist from Herod's point of view; those two stories form the Three Tales along with a story about an orphaned farm-girl who loves her parrot Loulou. This author of Bouvard and Pecuchet and "A Simple Heart" wrote about the university student Frederic Moreau in one novel and about the hapless surgeon Charles in another. The latter features the title character's affairs with Leon and Rodolphe. Name this French author of Sentimental Education and Madame Bovary.

The narrator of this story describes his friend's "delicate Hebrew model" and a chin whose lack of prominence suggests "a want of moral energy." That friend plays a "speaking guitar" that produces dirges as solemn as von Weber's last waltz. The narrator peers at a "black and lurid tarn" in order to dilute his apprehension, but it ends up deepening his dread. Its protagonist goes on to witness a strange whirlwind during a stormy night just after an incubus sits on his chest. A tale about Ethelred by Sir Launcelot Canning is read out loud by the narrator, who also hears about "The Haunted Mansion." A letter sent to the narrator summons him to the title structure, whose main vault is the site of an entombment, really a murder attempt, from which Madeleine escapes and dies with her brother Roderick. Identify this story that ends with the collapse of the title structure, written by Poe.
Fall of the House of Usher

The most quoted passage from this work imagines the restoration of "the guilty man's" "hopes of his youth," with "hands washed pure of blood." At the end of its second part, a "Notice to the Reader" summarizes the chronology of events, including the failure of Lord Desart's signatures to impress moneylenders. This work's title character enjoys the performances of the soprano Grassini and can't complete a publication on Ricardo. He frantically searches for a Malay man whom he had entertained in his house. The protagonist is taken care of by the prostitute Ann, who appears in a dream so terrifying to the narrator that he swears to never sleep again. This work addresses the "pleasures" and "pains" of the title substance, which was prescribed for neuralgic head pains. Identify this study of drug addiction based on the life of its author Thomas De Quincey.
Confessions of an English Opium Eater

One character created by this author escaped a lunatic asylum in Alexandria and built a hut in the forest. Another of his stories contains a turning circle of fire which torments the protagonist, who leaps to death after attempting to kill his lover, who is saved by Lotharr. In another story, an autobiography of a literate pet is mixed with the biography of his eventual master Johannes Kreisler. This author of "The Story of Serapion" and "The Life and Opinions of Kater Murr" wrote about a barometer salesman named Coppelius who torments Nathanael in one story, though his most familiar tale is about a certain soldier who is brought by Herr Drosselmeyer to fight the Mouse King. Name this German author of "The Sandman" and The Nutcracker.

This author wrote a play in which six shepherds and six foresters attend a contest that the schoolmaster Rombus moderates between Therion and Espilus for the hand of the title character. Another of his works is about "the companion of camps" that never "makes circles around your imagination;" that work was a response to Stephen Gosson's A School of Abuse. He wrote "Jove's strange tales attires" and "I sought fit words to paint the blackest face of woe." This author of The Lady of May wrote about the self-imposed seclusion of Basilius's royal family caused by a visit to the Delphic oracle in his prose narrative dedicated to the Countess of Pembroke. This author of A Defense of Poesy described "With how sad steps, ô Moon, thou climb'st the skies," in a collection of 108 sonnets and 11 songs. Identify this Elizabethan author of Arcadia and Astrophil and Stella.

The title character of one story written by this author cavorts with a member of her husband's former regiment, pawns her belongings to earn money for a newspaper ad, and jumps out of a window at the story's end. Another of his novels is about the mental disintegration of a government clerk who is not invited to Klara's birthday party but imagines her asking him to elope anyway. Besides writing "A Gentle Creature," this author wrote about a suicidal man who dreams he is on another planet after shooting himself in the heart. He wrote about a self-professed "dreamer" who roams St. Petersburg, falls in love with Nastenka, and suffers heartbreak at the end of four "White Nights." He described a man who goes to wish Zverkov off at a brothel where he meets Liza. Identify this Russian author whose shorter novels include The Double and Notes from the Underground.

An evil figure in this novel hides in a brothel whose twelve prostitutes are all executed. A delightful character in this novel declares that "religious fafaith" no longer "encodes the highest ass ass aspirations of human race." That character is shot by one protagonist, who is inspired by the suicide of his former mistress Rekha Merchant to throw his mountain-climbing wife from a high-rise. Several characters in this novel erect wax effigies of Margaret Thatcher, who is represented by the women Pamela Lovelace and Allelula Cone. The even-numbered chapters represent a dream that culminates in Ayesha leading a group of pilgrims through supposedly parted waters, in which they all drown. This novel opens an explosion on an Air India flight containing Gibreel Farishta and Saladin Chamcha. Identify this novel that brought a fatwa upon its author, Salman Rushdie.

This author's novel about Father Ignatius, Phillip Tempest, and their love interest, the lonely Rosamond Vivian, was not published until 1995. Abel Lamb and Sister Hope represent this author's father and mother in a story in which Timon Lion abandons Fruitlands to join the Shakers. The former novel, A Long Fatal Love Chase, was published under the pseudonym A.M. Barnard, and the latter story is "Transcendental Wild Oats." She wrote "A Forward Movement," "Obtaining Supplies," and "Off Duty" during her tenure as a nurse in the Union Army. She wrote Hospital Sketches and a novel about the poor German immigrant "Fritz" Bhaer, who marries the daughter of Marmee and sister of Amy, Beth, and Meg. Identify this creator of Jo March, who appears in Little Women.

One poem by this author features a lover who says "Night after Night, I die for you. How can you keep on sleeping?" This author described the inaccurate portrayal of a beautiful woman as a black fish in a work that explains that popular plays should not be shorter than five acts. One of his poems explains that when embarking on a journey to the Hydaspes or Caucasus, "poisoned arrows" aren't needed by the sinless man. He wrote a poem that describes grass reclaiming the field as snows scatter. Poems like "Tu ne quaesieris," "Integer Vitae," and "Diffugere Nives" comprise four books of his Odes. He coined the term "purple patch" while arguing that poetry should be like painting. "In medias res" was coined by, what Roman author who wrote Ars Poetica?

The namesake of this estate married the widow Beryl Muspratt. "An ancient, newly learned form of words" are uttered at the chapel of this estate at the end of the novel in which it appears. One inhabitant of this estate changes from being an ill-behaved schoolgirl to serving in the hospital bunks during the Spanish Civil War. That character's brother vomits through a window of this estate onto the ground floor room of his guest, and her sister marries a Canadian in the House of Commons named Rex Mottram. Cordelia and Julia live in this devoutly Catholic estate, home to the raging alcoholic Sebastian Flyte. Name this home of the Marchmain family that Charles Ryder "revisits" at the end of a novel by Evelyn Waugh.

In one chapter of this novel, the title character hits his head against a rock after falling off a burro. Earlier in that chapter, a lizard bites the thigh of the bald eagle Caligula, who is sent to a zoo in Indiana. The title character is matched up with the stutterer Friedl, the niece of the real estate hotshot Five Properties. Near the end of the novel, the title character is shacked up with the lunatic Basteshaw in a lifeboat and gets back together with his old flame Stella. He works for the CIO and assists Einhorn before going to Mexico with the hunting-obsessed Thea, for whom he keeps in mind the "respect, not love" maxim taught to him by his Machiavellian Grandma Lausch. The opening lines of this novel paraphrase Heraclitus and describe the title character as "an American, Chicago born." identify this bildungsroman set in the Great Depression, written by Saul Bellow.

One character in this novel repeats a series of French female names which are actually the seven French defensive positions at the Battle of Dien Bien Phu. That character often corresponds with his institutionalized mother Pelafina H. Lièvre, simply known by the letter P. This novel was expanded from a short story linking the disappearance of cats to the actions of a mysterious Redwood. Contradictory references to the "Five and a Half Minute Hallway" abound in this novel, which is the companion to its author's novella The Whalestoe Letters. A fictional study of a documentary, the Navidson Record, is written by the blind Zampanò, who is studied by the parlor employee Johnny Truant. This novel's cover is smaller than the pages and plenty of codes and a confusing index are present in most editions. Identify this academic satire, the magnum opus of Mark Z. Danielewski.

In one interlude in this play, a god representing Holiness is invoked to witness sacrilege. One character notes "this curl has fallen out of its proper place," instructing a king to "hold your head straight" as he cuts his hair. One character misses and plunges a knife into the shadow of his victim, who then conjures an earthquake and starts a fire. The protagonist of this play is told that Demeter is the god of solid nourishment by Tiresias, whose admonishment he ignores. This play opens with the revelation that Zeus had stitched the child of Semele into his own thigh; that child appears as a stranger to the Theban court of the protagonist, whose grandfather Cadmus becomes a snake. The protagonist is torn apart by the Maenads commanded by his mother Agave. Identify this play about Pentheus, who prohibits worship of Dionysus, a play by Euripides.

In one novel by this author, Roger finally confesses his love for Isolda and dies on the last drug-filled visit by Dick to the 14th century. In another novel by this author, Doctor Baker sees the title character on the last day of her life and is visited by the magistrate Colonel Julyan and her cousin and lover Jake Favell. She wrote about Mary Yellan, who goes to live with her Aunt Patience, wife of Joss, the villainous proprietor of the title establishment. In one novel, she wrote about a farmhand and his community who are attacked by a group of suicidal animals. This author of The House on the Strand and Jamaica Inn wrote about a dress ball ruined by the manipulation of Mrs. Danvers, the former housekeeper of the title character and Maxim de Winter. That novel by this author opens with the burning of the estate Manderley. Identify this English author of "The Birds" and Rebecca.
Dame Daphne du Maurier, Lady Browning

Near the end of this novel, Poorgrass and Coggan bicker during a performance of "The Royal Hippodrome Performance of Turpin's Ride to York and the Death of Black Bess." At its very end, the protagonist of this novel asks the men of the Malthouse to drink with him and his new wife, who had kept Liddy Smallbury as a confidante and had once locked herself in the attic. That woman is drawn to her first husband's prowess with the sword, which had diminished by the time that husband reappears, having disappeared following the ruination of a tombstone he built for his son and his lover Fanny Robin. Earlier in this novel, the central female sends an innocent valentine to William Boldwood and the central character's sheep all run off a cliff. Identify this novel about Sergeant Troy's relationship with Bathsheba Everdene, who finally marries Gabriel Oak, written by Thomas Hardy.

The film adaptation of this novel eliminated a character from Uppsala, who dies when the floor of a burning building collapses. A woman is compared to lines about beauty in the Song of Songs and to the Whore of Babylon by the narrator after and before he has sex with her. Another character in this novel brings girls from a local village in exchange for bits of meat; one of those women in particular was brought by Salvatore to Remigio, in direct opposition to the theory of Bernard Gui, an inquisitor. A head drowned in pig's blood, figures with blackened hands, and Malachi's murder are the handiwork of a character obsessed with the sequel to Aristotle's Poetics. That character, Jorge of Burgos, poisoned pages of books to commit his murders but was found out by William of Baskerville and his scribe, Adso of Melk. Identify this historical whodunit, written by Umberto Eco.

A maid who sleeps with the protagonist of this novel drowns herself when their tryst is brought to light. Other bad omens in this novel include the discovery of a purse embroidered with pornographic images and the blooming of a begonia tree out of season. Two parks in this novel are transformed into a magnificent pleasure grounds, the household of a woman who accepts bribes and charges interest at incredibly high rates. A sorceress is hired to bewitch that woman, Phoenix, whose actions cause two bailiffs to seize the property of the central family of this novel. This novel opens with the Great Void and its ruler Nugua, who, when repairing the Dome of Heaven, rejects a single jade stone which is found in the mouth of Paoyu. Identify this novel about the inhabitants of the Yungkuofu, the Chia family, a Qing dynasty novel by Cao Xueqin.

The title character of this novel is annoyed to find that he has no matches for his pipe and recalls his lost first love, a woman named Puss Flanagan. That character later encounters a man who was imprisoned for calling a woman's hair red instead of auburn; he frees that man and sends him off to his "Man Factory." Near the end of this novel, the title character mutters "Hello-Central" in his sleep, thus naming his child. He also suffers from "the interdict," but his rival fails to kill him and instead electrocutes himself. A bunch of ogres who have kidnapped maidens in this novel turn out to be pigs, although the protagonist's wife Sandy is fooled. An "interested stranger" is told the events of this novel, which include the foiling of a solar eclipse and a crowbar blow suffered by Hank Morgan, transporting him to sixth century Camelot. Identify this satire of chivalry, written by Mark Twain.
A Connecticut Yankee in King Arthur's Court

One character in this novel, Mr. Smales, is met at the Whitby Cemetery just after one character records his diary on a phonograph and his wife's friend practices typing on a new typewriter. Another character in this novel is a simple American from Texas who courts a central character, who writes a letter to her friend lamenting that she can't marry three men at once. The antagonist of this novel rides a ship called the Czarina Catherine and calls back three underlings called the Weird Sisters at this novel's opening. The sight of a wolf leaping through a window causes a fatal heart attack for the mother of a character who begins sleepwalking after seeing a cargo of boxes of earth shipped to the house of the title character, who attempts to suck the blood of Mina. Holmwood drives a stake through the heart of Lucy Westerna in this novel, in which Van Helsing cleans out the estate of a Transylvanian count. Identify this novel about a vampire, the masterpiece of Bram Stoker.

In this novel, a grandfather tells his son that it is a sin to prefer one dish to another because "there are people who are hungry." This novel's narrator compares his "internal no" and "the void" with the Buddha, which he studies about just as the title character compares the Virgin Mary to the object of his affection. That woman spends the night with the narrator and causes a jealous suitor to drown himself in the ocean, leading to her own stoning. The title character often dances and plays his santuri, which he uses to entertain and persuade several monks into letting him use the timber from their forest. The murder of the Widow occurs just before an aged hotel-owning harlot marries the title character, who had first met the narrator at a cafe in Piraeus and serves under him as an employee of a lignite mine in Crete. Madame Hortense dies at the end of, what masterwork of Nikos Kazantzakis?

One work by this thinker discusses how the "possible powers" of an agent are not necessarily moral, and attempts to define potentialities in terms of the two concepts of "fixed" and "intrinsic" ends. In addition to "Time and Individuality," this man posited that nature is a system of "possible starting points and opportunities rather than final ends" in another work. He responded to a Walter Lippmann book by positing that the populus cannot be transformed into the title entity until the fruits of scientific knowledge can be easily disseminated. This author of The Quest for Certainty wrote a work that attacks the business mind for leading to a sense of self-satisfaction in the title form of government, which is improved by offering a progressive form of the titular pedagogy to children. Name this American philosopher who penned The Public and Its Problems and Democracy and Education.

The mountain ranges around one city in this novel are described as "papier-mache" in a poem about the "doldrums" of that city, home to a staging of Fidelio attended by the main characters. One character takes up a job at a parking garage and another works as a security guard in a barracks for construction workers. The protagonist tries and fails to seduce the sex-addicted Rita Bettencourt, but exercises restraint with Lee Ann, the sulky girlfriend of his prep school friend Remi Boncoeur. After spending fifteen days with Terry, the protagonist joins Stan Shepherd in a marijuana-filled sojourn to Mexico City, years after he leaves New York City for Denver to meet up with Dean Moriarty. Neal Cassady and William S Boroughs are fictionalized in, what autobiographical novel about Sal Paradise, written by Jack Kerouac?

One character in this play thinks that a villain is named Deformed and alludes to a "worm-eaten tapestry" in which Hercules's codpiece is as big as his club. Another character promises to "eat all of his killing," referring to the casualties inflicted in battle by her eventual lover. That lover muses that instead of the sign "Here is a good horse to hire," there should be a sign pointing to him as a married man, should marriage come to pass. This play contains a ghost character in the role of Innogen, whose husband hears the fanciful tale of the Watch, who is supervised by Verges. Another character seduces Margaret in the guise of Hero, who is besmirched by the "Bastard Prince" Don John. Leonato governs Messina, whose constables are led by Dogberry in this play that ends with a fickle couple finally confessing their love. Identify this Shakespeare play about Beatrice and Benedick.

One poet who wrote in this language described "soul of antiquity/Gone gray with age and rage" and wondered "How lonely what is left to you must be!" Another poet who wrote in this language asked "do you remember/the moments in your mortal life/when beauty still shone in your sidelong, laughing eyes" in one poem and pondered "it was always dear to me, this solitary hill" in another. Another poet wrote about "the day the sun's rays turned white" as the day he fell in love and wrote about "a rain of bitter tears fall[ing] from my face" because she never reciprocated. "To Sylvia," and "The Infinite" were written in this language, which was used to write another author's "Guide to the Holy Land," "On Famous Men," a verse epic about Scipio Africanus, and hymns to Laura in his Canzoniere. Identify this language that names a particular type of sonnet coined by the author Petrarch.

One character in this novel imagines that his eye has been gouged out by a carabinieri who had jailed him for violently settling a dispute with a taxi driver and policeman. One quarrel early in this novel occurs at a party and erupts into a duel in which several shots are fired but hit neither Mr. McKisko nor a professional soldier who later leaves Russia after completing a romance. The latter character, Tommy Barban, begins an affair with a woman who was involved incestuously with her father, causing a breakdown that put her in a mental hospital in Zurich. A murder precipitated by composer Abe North ruins the protagonist's marriage with his first wife, who like his second wife is also named Nicole. This novel opens when the star of Daddy's Girl, Rosemary Hoyt, meets a psychologist on a beach in Southern France. Identify this novel about Dick Diver, written by F. Scott Fitzgerald.

One poet from this country debuted poems like "Sadness" and "Colloque Sentimental" at its Week of Modern Art, wrote a novel about an "emperor of the forest" who seduces Si, and led the "Group of Five" with an unrelated poet with the same surname, Oswald. One novel set in this country is about Galileo Gall, who sexually exploits Jurema, the lover of a narrator known only as The Nearsighted Journalist. That novel was inspired by an account of a civil war in this country known as the Rebellion in the Backlands. One author from this country wrote a novel whose title character's wife Capitu cheats on him with his best friend, as well as a novel which contains the pickpocket Quincas Borba. The setting of The War of the End of the World, Dom Casmurro, and The Posthumous Memoirs of Bras Cubas, identify this country whose Portuguese-language novelists include Machado de Assis.
